Rights of Man

by Thomas Paine

|Rights of Man is a work of political science by Thomas Paine arguing for political rights of the people, including the right of revolution when governments do not respect the people's rights.
Bibliographic notes
The first part of Rights of Man was published in 1791, in response to a work by Edmund Burke critical of the French Revolution. The second part was first published in 1792. Most editions published after Paine's death in 1809 include both parts.

"The Rights of Man" by Thomas Paine is a political work published in two parts in 1791 and 1792. Written in defense of the French Revolution against Edmund Burke's conservative attack, it argues that governments exist solely to protect natural human rights and that revolution is justified when they fail this purpose. Paine challenges hereditary monarchy and aristocracy, proposing radical reforms including a written constitution, elimination of noble titles, progressive taxation, and subsidized education for the poor.
